mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 2% for two consecutive months signals a prolonged easing cycle, which reduces risk-free rates and boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2.0% for two consecutive months ending on decision date
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than baseline during triggered episodes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year acceleration in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1 growth) above 3% coincident with rising housing starts (HOUST) signals robust domestic demand, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY growth > 3% AND HOUST > previous 6-month average at decision date
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above baseline when both GDPC1 and HOUST conditions are met (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and cost-push inflation, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5.0% for three consecutive months ending on decision date
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline during triggered episodes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its prior 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which depresses earnings expectations and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for four consecutive months ending on decision date
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline during triggered episodes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by 75 basis points or more within a single month signals an aggressive tightening stance, which raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by ≥ 0.75% in one month relative to prior month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline after such a rate hike (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal income (PAYEMS) and retail sales (RSAFS) below their 12-month moving averages signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS < 12-month MA AND RSAFS < 12-month MA at decision date
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline when both PAYEMS and RSAFS are below their 12-month MAs (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points in one month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by > 0.50 pp in one month relative to prior month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline after such an unemployment spike (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous deceleration in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) below their respective 6-month moving averages signals broad-based supply-side weakness, which depresses earnings and capital expenditure, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 6-month MA AND HOUST < 6-month MA at decision date
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than baseline when both INDPRO and HOUST are below their 6-month MAs (p > 0.10).
